issue: Gnomic aorist/injunctive déh₃t, térst beside presents (accepted convention). h₁yód 'when' as in earlier batches.
h₂erh₃wṓd is ablative ('from the arable'); 'burns the arable land' needs the accusative h₂erh₃wóm (as in 7f8c64c5). Also h₂erh₃wós is an adjective 'arable' used substantivally (minor).
bʰebʰih₂ḗr perfect 'have taken fright' = 'are afraid' is fine. súHes 'pigs' is a cap substitute for cattle but weather-lore about pigs sensing wind is plausible.

memn̥té is IMP.2PL addressed to a single vocative népot 'grandson'; needs IMP.2SG memn̥dʰí (the engine builds it). The 2sg prohibitive mē h₃sléydʰs that follows confirms the singular addressee. h₃sléydʰs 'slip' for 'go astray' is a stretched sense.
stunddʰí 'push' for 'strike' is a stretched sense; English repeats 'strike' (PIE once). dʰh₂bʰrós 'craftsman' for 'smith' fine.

dʰégʷʰome is PST.1PL 'we burned' (transitive, péh₂wr̥ object); English 'The fire was burning' needs 3sg intransitive dʰégʷʰet with péh₂wr̥ subject (cf. 716daa9e péh₂wr̥ dʰégʷʰeti). Person and meaning change.
kúdʰe 'where' for 'where from'; péruns abl. carries the 'from' in the answer. gʰóstis 'stranger/guest' fine.

Reflexive swā́s in a clause whose subject is ǵʰwḗr 'beast' reads 'the beast's own sheep'; the possessor is the herdsman, so a non-reflexive (genitive anaphor) is expected. swós in the nominative 'his own horse' is a looser, attested 'own' use. Otherwise the agreement (neuter h₁wésu, ń̥dʰgʷʰitom with ḱléwos) is correct.
n̥bʰróm 'rain-cloud' for 'rain' is a lexicon-driven gloss shift. Vocative + 3sg optative h₂wr̥syéh₁t 'Father Sky, may it rain' is fine.
Gnomic aorist h₂wérst for 'it rains' (accepted). gʷm̥sḱéti 'walks' for 'comes' fine.
lelikʷḗr perfect 'are gone'; tríns h₁íns 'three of them'; h₁éyes m. for gʷṓws m. séh₂gyet 'tracked' used absolutely; widóm 'I saw' for 'I found' is close enough.
n̥bʰróns is ACC.PL; 'Rain-cloud, come!' needs the vocative singular ń̥bʰre, which the same item uses later (ń̥bʰre litdʰí).
Feminine anaphor h₁íh₂n̥s for sheep correct. ǵénh₁tōr 'begetter, parent' is a cap-adjacent but accurate choice.
'Mother Earth, feed the cattle!' — PIE h₂éle has no object: 'the cattle' is not rendered (PIE and English differ in content). Also vocative dʰéǵʰom méh₂ter beside nom. dʰéǵʰōm méh₂tēr is correct.
Enclitic nos in second position after dyéw is Wackernagel-correct; it reads 'our' with the herd. -wē 'nor' after mē-clauses fine. Subject of h₁édih₁t (the herd) is implicit.
Middle Hrumptór 'breaks (intr.)' and 2pl prohibitive mē h₃slidʰté are well formed.
Tier 1 line (King and God), faithful to source notation: unaccented h₁estu.
yúH nogʷṓs: nogʷṓs is masculine NOM.PL, but the addressees are the sheep (h₂ówis f., cf. h₁íh₂n̥s in 1550eeb9); needs feminine nogʷéh₂es. Agreement error.
pótni 'mistress, lady' for 'wife' is a stretched sense. Grammar fine: kú 'where', h₁édn̥t PST.3PL, h₂lékseti.
Narten imperfect h₁ḗdt, root aorist h₂wést 'dawned', h₁éǵʰs ... ǵʰéyt 'drove out' all fine.

Grammar fine (mē + injunctive h₂éǵes, acc. of goal pérwr̥, ḱóymom). But the cap substitutes make the lore odd: 'do not drive the pigs to the mountain', 'lead the son home' in a weather rule stand where calves/cattle are expected. pérwr̥ is ambiguous between 'ford' and 'rock'.
Tier 1 Schleicher-type line in source notation (unaccented, no laryngeals).
Grammar fine (dedh₃té 2pl reduplicated present, mē bʰih₂té). wr̥h₁ḗn 'lamb' sipping cows' milk stands in for a calf: an unnatural cap substitute.
wédni is LOC.SG 'in the water'; 'Carry the water' needs the accusative wódr̥, which the next sentence uses (wódr̥ limnés bʰére).
Locative of goal nébʰesi 'into cloud'; séngʷt 'sank' gnomic aorist; ḱéyor middle.
kʷékʷlos for 'wagon' in the second clause is the inherited dual sense (Gk κύκλα, Toch. kukäl). wéndʰetor middle 'turns' fine.
Thematic imperatives bʰéwdʰe, spéḱye, ḱléwse; prohibitive mē légʰs with root aorist injunctive.
